# Fransys 0.22.4

> Fransys is a Python toolkit for authoring electrical cabinet and harness designs and producing their schematics, parts lists and manufacturing exports from one model.

Version 0.22.4. Everything here is also in one file: https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/llms-full.txt.

## Guide

- [Overview](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/index.md): Fransys is a Python toolkit for authoring electrical cabinet and harness designs and producing their schematics, parts lists and manufacturing exports from one model. This page lists every consumer task with its one spelling, then the install and the shape of a script.
- [Parts](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/parts/index.md): A part library is a Python data package: TOML files describing parts, and no code. Fransys never reads a spreadsheet or a manufacturer's own format directly; every part your design uses comes from an installed library written against the part-file contract. This page covers starting a design from a library, the typed parts module, class codes, linting and load failures. The contract itself is the "Part file contract" page of the site, at the version you installed. Read it before you write a library.
- [Authoring a design](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/authoring/index.md): This page teaches how to write a design with `fr.design`: places, function blocks, devices, terminal strips, wires, cables, supplies, PLC requests and layout advice. Each task has one spelling, shown first written out and then with Python around it.
- [Wiring a design](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/series/index.md): This page teaches how to wire a design: `d.series` along a current path, branches and changeovers, cables, wire colours and earth pins. It follows `authoring.md`, which holds the places, devices and strips these calls join.
- [The required-drawn ledger](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/drawn-ledger/index.md): `fr.derive.required_drawn` lists what a drawing of a model must show: both ends of each conductor, and each function that gets a symbol. Each row is drawn, carried by a named reason, or an error.
- [Detail calls](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/detail/index.md): Each call here is for a case no core call writes. Try the core call first (`authoring.md`): a series pairs poles and takes the next free terminal or core, and layout reads its structure. `d.detail` is a `fr.Detail` handle, as `d.layout` is a `fr.Layout`.
- [Harnesses](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/harnesses/index.md): This page teaches how to add a harness to a design with `d.harness`, and how its cables and plugs print. It follows `authoring.md`, which holds the rest of the authoring calls.
- [Units](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/units/index.md): A unit is a released, independently built part of a design: a board, a cabinet, a box, anything built and delivered on its own revision. This page shows how to write one, mark its interface, record its revisions and nest it in a cabinet. A cabinet is itself a unit: it holds components, units and wires, and it is never split into places.
- [Building a design](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/build/index.md): `fr.build`, `fr.check` and `fr.write` are the three pipeline functions. `build` takes the design (and any documents), merges them into a model and runs the passes, the validators, and layout when there is a document. `check` collects every finding about a built model, including some `build` never sees. `write` writes the model's exports to a directory. If any finding is an `ERROR` it raises `BuildFailedError`, writes no export, and removes the exports an earlier `write` left there. `check` also places the system overview (`overview.html`) and returns its findings. `settings=fr.settings(...)` sets the build's paper (settings.md).
- [Documents](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/documents/index.md): A `Document` record is what turns an authored design into a printable deliverable. `fr.document` authors one such record as a `Draft`. Pass it to `fr.build(d, doc)` next to the design `d`; the model does the rest at layout and write time.
- [Reading a model](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/reading/index.md): `fransys.derive` is the read side of a model: every designation, table, row and rating a script might need already has a function here. Layout, render and every output call the same ones. Every function's docstring is its full reference. What follows is a short tour of the read surface: enough to know what is there and how to reach for it.
- [Layout numbers](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/layout-numbers/index.md): This page lists every keyword of `d.layout.profile`: what it does, its house value, its effect on the drawing, and when to change it. A gap is in grid units `G`; eight `G` make one symbol module.
- [Reading: rows, columns and printed texts](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/reading-rows/index.md): This page covers `fr.derive`, the facade's read-only layer. It holds the column accessors of the list outputs and the row types they are built from. It also holds the row functions, and the texts and order keys every list shares. Use these to read a model yourself and get the same numbers, text and order the outputs print.
- [Reading: records, lookups and ratings](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/reading-records/index.md): This page covers the records that describe a model's structure, the lookups that find them, and the ratings and currents that say what a circuit may carry. Each record type has a table function that returns every record of that type, keyed by id. Every name here is reached as `fr.derive.NAME`.
- [Keywords and handles](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/keywords/index.md): This page lists the public names of the facade's handles and signal types, then the keyword arguments of the record constructors. The keywords of the `d.*` calls are in `keywords-design.md`, those of the handle methods and layout hints in `keywords-handles.md`, those of the `fr.*` functions in `keywords-output.md`.
- [Keywords of the d calls](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/keywords-design/index.md): This page has one table for each `d.*` and `d.detail.*` call: each keyword, its default, its effect and an example. A call that takes only `*args` has no table; one sentence says what it takes.
- [Keywords of the handle methods and layout hints](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/keywords-handles/index.md): This page has one table for each handle method and each `d.layout.*` hint: each named keyword, its default, its effect and an example fragment. A call that takes only `*args` has no table, and one sentence says what it takes.
- [Keywords of the fr functions](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/keywords-output/index.md): This page has one table for each `fr.*` function: each named keyword, its default, its effect and an example call fragment. A call that takes only `*args` has no table, and one sentence says what it takes.
- [Settings](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/settings/index.md): This page holds the settings of one build: `fr.settings`, the consumer's TOML file, the paper per drawing type, and the `SettingsError` a wrong key raises. Every build uses our defaults until you pass `settings=`.
- [Moving to 0.22](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-0.22/index.md): This page lists each call that 0.22 adds, changes or removes, with the old spelling and the new one.
- [Moving to 0.20](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-0.20/index.md): This page lists each call that 0.20 adds or changes, with the old spelling and the new one.
- [Moving to 0.19](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-0.19/index.md): This page lists each call that 0.19 moves or changes, with the old spelling and the new one. A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below.
- [Moving to 0.16 and 0.17](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-0.16-and-0.17/index.md): This page covers a move from 0.15 to 0.16, to 0.17, or across both. If you are on 0.16, read the 0.17 section only. Nothing in `fr.__all__` is removed or renamed. A stored model written by 0.15 or 0.16 no longer loads.
- [Moving to 0.15](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-0.15/index.md): This page lists each call, name and finding that 0.15 changes, with the old spelling and the new one. A consumer script that used an old spelling changes as below. The version is read with `importlib.metadata.version("fransys")`; there is no `fr.__version__`.
- [Moving to 0.14](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-0.14/index.md): This page lists every `fr.derive` name 0.14 removes, and what to use instead. `fr.derive` now holds the names a consumer needs to read a model, and every one has a guide entry. The rest stay in the workspace for layout, render and the outputs. A consumer script that used a removed name changes as below.
- [Finding codes](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/findings/index.md): Every code Fransys can emit, with severity, stage, who acts, meaning and fix, on five pages by source.
- [Finding codes: validators, build and release](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/findings-validators/index.md): Codes the model checks and the library load emit. Who acts is explained in `findings.md`.
- [Finding codes: build, release and verify](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/findings-release/index.md): Codes the build, `release`, `verify` and the baseline check emit. Who acts is explained in `findings.md`.
- [Finding codes: layout and render](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/findings-render/index.md): Codes the layout and the drawing stage emit. Who acts is explained in `findings.md`.
- [Finding codes: PDF](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/findings-pdf/index.md): Codes the PDF output emits. Who acts is explained in `findings.md`.
- [Finding codes: KiCad](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/findings-kicad/index.md): Codes the KiCad import emits. Who acts is explained in `findings.md`.
- [Finding codes: part files](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/findings-parts/index.md): Codes the part-file lint emits, at `fr.lint` and when `fr.design` or `fr.parts` loads a library. Who acts is explained in `findings.md`.
- [Examples](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/examples/index.md): Worked examples of whole circuits, each shown the easy way and the efficient way, and a pointer to a full build script outside this repository. All parts are from `demo_parts`.
- [Moving to 0.6](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-0.6/index.md): This page lists every change a 0.5 consumer script or part file must make for 0.6. Each entry gives the 0.5 spelling, the 0.6 spelling and one line of why. The 0.5 spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.
- [KiCad](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/kicad/index.md): Fransys writes a KiCad netlist for each board in your model. This page shows how to import it into a KiCad 9 board, which settings to use, and how to start a part file from a KiCad symbol.
- [Moving to Fransys](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/moving-to-fransys/index.md): This page lists every change a script written for version 0.6.1 under the old name must make for Fransys 0.7.0. Each entry gives the old spelling, the new one and one line of why. The old spellings sit in text blocks: they no longer run.
- [Drawing well](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/drawing/index.md): Layout draws the structure you author and invents none. This page says what layout reads, how to author a cabinet that draws readably, which numbers change its size, and which findings mean the design lacks structure.
- [Reading the pages as numbers](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/readability/index.md): `fr.readability(result)` returns a `DrawnReading`: one `DrawnPageReading` row for each page the build drew, in `.pages`. Both types are in `fr.derive`. The same model gives equal rows, so compare a page between revisions by its rows. It writes no file, `fr.write` does not emit it, and it lays nothing out again.
- [The system overview](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/overview/index.md): `overview.html` is one file that `fr.write(result, out_dir)` puts beside the PDFs. It needs no network and no server: open it in a browser. This page says how to read it.
- [For coding agents](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/guide/AGENTS/index.md): The official Fransys documentation is the site, one version per release. Paste this block into your project's `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` so every agent that works on the project finds it:

## Part files

- [Part file contract](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/contracts/part-file/index.md): Version 1. Parts are data, not code: TOML files in a data package that the loader reads and the lint checks.
- [Part file connectors](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/contracts/part-file-connectors/index.md): This page holds the `[function.connector]` table of the part-file contract. It is read with `part-file.md`, which holds the rest of the contract.

- [Overview](https://olejbondahl.github.io/fransys/0.22.4/api/index.md): Every name each public surface exports.
